Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Topeka KS
623 PM CDT Thu Oct 8 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

-A stretch of seasonably warm weather continues through the weekend
 and into next week.

-Conditions remain dry until a pattern shift brings low pressure
 toward the area early/mid next week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 229 PM CDT Thu Oct 8 2026

Water vapor imagery and H5 analysis at 18Z shows high pressure 
stretching from the Great Basin eastward over the Red River and 
Lower Mississippi River Valleys. Northwest flow exists north of the 
broad ridge, and Hurricane Isaias continues to churn in the central 
Gulf. Another relatively warm day is underway with temps in the mid 
80s, compared to our low 70 averages. Weak WAA with southwesterly 
winds will keep conditions warm tomorrow with temperatures expected 
to quickly warming into the upper 80s. The mid-level synoptic 
pattern across the CONUS shifts and becomes more amplified this 
weekend as a deep low pressure system digs over the PNW and dives 
southward over CA. In the meantime, Hurricane Isaias will quickly 
work inland through AL/MS and into TN. Conditions closer to home 
don't change much this weekend, except that southwest winds will be a
bit stronger.

Wet weather still looks to return to the forecast, along with more 
seasonable temperatures next week as the aforementioned western 
storm system evolves and ejects toward the Central Plains. Long 
range guidance continues to show varying solutions, however, there 
remains some signal for an initial round of rain and storms on 
Tuesday with a surface boundary draped across the area, and the 
possibility of strong storms developing Wednesday or Wednesday 
night. Temperatures would then trend noticeably cooler by the end of 
next week as a surface ridge builds in from the north.

&&

.AVIATION /00Z TAFS THROUGH 00Z FRIDAY/...
Issued at 616 PM CDT Thu Oct 8 2026

VFR conditions are forecast. Light winds from the SSE this evening
gradually veer through the period, picking up from the SW Friday
morning and increasing to 10-15 kts for most of the afternoon. Can't
entirely rule out the possibility of shallow ground fog in the river
valley at TOP around sunrise, but the window looks brief and Td 
depressions could be a bit more than we saw this morning. 
Additionally, 20-25 kt wind a few hundred feet above the surface 
lowers confidence in formation, but future shifts will need to 
monitor.
